dimensions.name: Customer Definition
dimensions.pass_criteria: A specific named persona, role, segment, or job title is identified. The reader knows exactly who has this problem.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Customer is vague, such as users, teams, enterprises, people, or customers without further specificity. A new team member could not describe the customer after reading this.

dimensions.name: Problem Evidence
dimensions.pass_criteria: The problem is specific and evidenced with a concrete pain, current workaround, frequency, cost, or quote. The reader understands why this matters now.
dimensions.fail_criteria: The problem is generic, such as frustrating, slow, or no good solution, without specifics. No evidence shows that this is a real, acute pain.

dimensions.name: Customer Benefit
dimensions.pass_criteria: The customer knows exactly what they get. The benefit is concrete, specific, directly tied to the problem, and the headline and solution paragraph agree.
dimensions.fail_criteria: The benefit is vague, such as easier, faster, or better, without saying what specifically changes for the customer.

dimensions.name: Spokesperson Quote
dimensions.pass_criteria: The quote explains the insight, mission, or opportunity in language a real person could say.
dimensions.fail_criteria: The quote is generic launch or marketing language and could be copied onto any product announcement.

dimensions.name: Customer Quote
dimensions.pass_criteria: The quote is specific and believable. It describes a real outcome or reaction in the customer's voice, with placeholders clearly marked when not yet validated.
dimensions.fail_criteria: The quote invents unsupported metrics or outcomes without marking them as placeholders, or it uses generic praise.

dimensions.name: Question Quality
dimensions.pass_criteria: Every question represents a genuine challenge a skeptical customer would raise about risk, cost, workflow change, data, competition, or failure modes.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Questions are softballs, leading questions that assume a positive answer, or questions a marketing team would write.

dimensions.name: Answer Completeness
dimensions.pass_criteria: Every question has a substantive answer or is explicitly marked open with a named owner.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Questions are unanswered, marked TBD, or marked open without a named owner.

dimensions.name: No Evasive Answers
dimensions.pass_criteria: Each answer directly resolves the question asked, or names uncertainty with an open item.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Answers deflect, restate the question, use vague future promises, or use marketing language to avoid a hard truth.

dimensions.name: Coverage of Critical Concerns
dimensions.pass_criteria: The FAQ covers the customer concerns most likely to block adoption: data/privacy, workflow change, cost/value, failure modes, trust/support, and alternatives.
dimensions.fail_criteria: A critical adoption concern is missing, and the omission would leave a reasonable customer concern unanswered.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Coverage
dimensions.pass_criteria: The FAQ includes hard questions from at least three stakeholder perspectives: engineering, business/leadership, and legal/compliance where applicable.
dimensions.fail_criteria: One or more stakeholder perspectives are absent or represented only by softball questions. Engineering questions that cover only the happy path are insufficient.

dimensions.name: Answer Completeness
dimensions.pass_criteria: Every question has a substantive answer or is explicitly marked open with a named owner.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Questions are unanswered, marked TBD, or open without an owner.

dimensions.name: Blocker Identification
dimensions.pass_criteria: Any open item that would prevent safe build handoff, such as legal risk, missing capability, unresolved dependency, or compliance requirement, is flagged as a blocker.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Build-blocking issues are buried as normal open items, omitted, or left for engineering to infer.

dimensions.name: No Evasive Answers
dimensions.pass_criteria: Hard questions receive direct answers, explicit open items, or explicit blockers.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Hard questions receive vague, aspirational, or deflecting answers instead of honest responses or open/blocker flags.

dimensions.name: Requirement Traceability
dimensions.pass_criteria: Every requirement traces to the press release, external FAQ, internal FAQ, or named open item.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Requirements appear without source artifact IDs or source rationale.

dimensions.name: Testable Acceptance Criteria
dimensions.pass_criteria: Acceptance criteria use observable given/when/then behavior.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Acceptance criteria are vague, subjective, or cannot be tested.

dimensions.name: Edge Case Coverage
dimensions.pass_criteria: Key failure modes, boundary cases, and recovery paths are named.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Only the happy path is described.

dimensions.name: Non-Functional Requirements
dimensions.pass_criteria: Performance, security/privacy, reliability, observability, accessibility, and scale/cost are covered or explicitly open.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Non-functional requirements are missing without open items.

dimensions.name: Open Item Propagation
dimensions.pass_criteria: Open items and blockers from prior stages are preserved with owner and impact.
dimensions.fail_criteria: Open items disappear, are softened, or are worked around silently.
